task.title: Show and manage task dependencies in the web UI
task.description:
Make task dependencies visible and safely editable throughout the local web app. Board cards show prerequisite progress and clearly identify Ready tasks that remain ineligible. Existing and New Task views use the same responsive layout: title and flexible description in the main column, with status, priority, labels, Depends On, and Blocks in a compact sidebar that becomes a single column on narrow screens.

Users can add or remove dependencies in either direction through accessible integrated comboboxes. Existing-task mutations are immediate Git-durable bodyless dependency requests. New Task keeps relationship drafts client-side, creates the task exactly once, then persists each captured relationship through the nested endpoints. Partial successes remain durable; failed drafts stay visible with Retry and Remove actions, and refresh recovery cannot repeat task creation. Relationship controls lock during submission, polling reconciles active and deleted candidates without losing drafts, and detached async completion cannot navigate away from a newer route.

Missing or tombstoned relationship targets remain visible as unavailable or deleted and remain removable. Self-dependencies, cycles, missing candidates, stale data, and server failures surface actionable errors without discarding form state. The server remains loopback-only and preserves versioned JSON and error contracts.

Acceptance criteria:
- Board cards with dependencies show completed versus total prerequisites and distinguish Ready-but-ineligible tasks; cards without dependencies remain unchanged.
- Existing and New Task views share the desktop sidebar and responsive mobile layout, preserving vertical space for the description.
- Both Depends On and Blocks show resolved task information and explicit fallbacks for missing or tombstoned targets.
- Users can add and remove relationships in either direction from existing tasks and include both directions while creating a task.
- New-task relationship persistence creates once, attempts all captured edges, preserves partial successes, and supports safe retry or removal of failures.
- Accessible keyboard behavior, live feedback, bounds-aware combobox placement, route ownership, polling, and durable mutation recovery have executable coverage.
- Focused web and core tests, the full Go suite, go vet, production build, and full-branch diff checks pass.
